title: Crispy Chickpea Bowls with Lemony Yogurt (stovetop)
source: adapted from [Warm Chickpea Bowls With Lemony Yogurt — Bon Appétit, Andy Baraghani](https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/warm-chickpea-bowls-with-lemony-yogurt) (4.8★/110)

bowls.name: Lemony yogurt
bowls.arrowText: stirred at step 2, → bowls at step 7

bowls.name: Lemony salad
bowls.arrowText: tossed at step 2, → on top at step 7

bowls.name: Chickpeas
items: 1 15-oz can chickpeas (no-salt-added), rinsed and patted very dry

bowls.name: Bloom
bowls.arrowText: → cleared spot in pan at step 5
items: 1½ tsp ground cumin (a little extra stands in for the original's coriander)

bowls.name: Kale
items: 1 small bunch kale, stems stripped, torn large

stationExtras.label: Stove-side
items: ~3 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided (2 Tbsp at step 3, a little at step 5, thread to finish)

steps.text: **Mise — no heat (~15 min).** Work the bowl map above — everything prepped and beside the stove before heat goes on. **Reset before ignition:** dump the garbage bowl, wash knife & board, wipe the counter. Once the burner clicks on, the knife is done.
**Sauces — no heat (~2 min).** Stir Bowl ① (yogurt + lemon). Toss Bowl ② (cucumber, onion, parsley + lemon).
**Preheat — MEDIUM-HIGH (~2 min).** Empty stainless pan until a water drop skates; add 2 Tbsp olive oil, swirl to a shimmer.

**Crisp the chickpeas — stay on MEDIUM-HIGH (8–10 min).** Bowl ③ in a single layer; leave 2–3 min between stirs. Done when: deep golden, skins splitting, rattly-sounding. *Dead minutes: rinse the colander and board, set out the 2 serving bowls.*
steps.leadIn: Crisp the chickpeas — stay on MEDIUM-HIGH (8–10 min).

steps.text: **Bloom — drop to MEDIUM (30–45 sec).** Bowl ④ (cumin + garlic) in a little oil in a cleared spot until fragrant, then stir through (garlic goes in late so it doesn't burn).
**Kale — stay on MEDIUM (2–3 min).** Bowl ⑤ in; toss until wilted with crisp edges. **OFF HEAT**, squeeze of lime.
**Plate — no heat.** Yogurt down, chickpea-kale over, lemony salad on top, thread of olive oil.

title: Turkey Marinara Skillet (jar-stretch, low-sodium)
source: Adapted from "Amazing Ground Turkey Tomato Sauce" (Allrecipes, 4.6★) — https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/236982/amazing-ground-turkey-tomato-sauce/

bowls.name: Spices
bowls.arrowText: → pan at step 5, on the aromatics

bowls.name: Tomatoes
items: 1 cup jarred marinara (the open jar — measure it, don't pour free)

stationExtras.label: Stove-side
items: 1 lb 93% ground turkey (straight from fridge pack)
the cooked pasta + a splash of water to loosen

steps.text: **Mise — set the station (no heat, ~2 min).** Garbage bowl, damp towel under board, hand towel, landing plate. Read the steps through. Once the burner clicks on, the knife is done.
steps.leadIn: Mise — set the station (no heat, ~2 min).

steps.text: **Mise — fill the bowls (no heat, ~8 min).** Work the map above; line bowls up ① → ④. **Reset before ignition:** dump garbage bowl, wash knife & board, wipe counter.
steps.leadIn: Mise — fill the bowls (no heat, ~8 min).

steps.text: **Preheat — MEDIUM-HIGH, empty stainless pan, 2–3 min.** Water-drop test: bead-and-skitter. Add the olive oil, wait for a full shimmer. *Dead minute: fill the sink with hot soapy water.*
steps.leadIn: Preheat — MEDIUM-HIGH, empty stainless pan, 2–3 min.

steps.text: **Brown the turkey — stay on MEDIUM-HIGH, ~5–6 min.** Add the turkey and press it into one flat layer with the spoon — then **don't touch for 3–4 min**. You want a deep brown crust underneath (that's fond forming — flavor, not burning). Then crumble into bite-size pieces and cook 2 min more. Done when: no pink, brown crusty bits on the pan bottom.
steps.leadIn: Brown the turkey — stay on MEDIUM-HIGH, ~5–6 min.

steps.text: **Aromatics — drop to MEDIUM, ~3–4 min.** Onion into the turkey, stir until it softens and picks up color. Garlic + the spice bowl in, stir 30–60 sec until fragrant — not brown.

**Tomatoes — stay on MEDIUM to a bubble, then MEDIUM-LOW, 15 min.** Pour in bowl ③, scrape the fond up off the bottom (it dissolves into the sauce). Lazy simmer, lid off, stirring occasionally, until it thickens to spoon-track. *Dead minutes: wash the board & spoon rest, set out meal-prep containers.*
steps.leadIn: Tomatoes — stay on MEDIUM to a bubble, then MEDIUM-LOW, 15 min.

steps.text: **Pasta in — stay on MEDIUM-LOW, ~2 min.** Fold the cooked pasta in with a splash of water to loosen; toss until the pasta is hot and glossed with sauce.
steps.leadIn: Pasta in — stay on MEDIUM-LOW, ~2 min.

steps.text: **Balance — OFF HEAT.** Taste. Flat? A small splash of balsamic and a grind of pepper — never salt; the jar already brought it.

**Plate.** Shallow bowl, mound high in the center. One dollop (2 tbsp) ricotta on top — don't stir it in, let it melt streaky. Parsley from height, wipe the rim. Remaining 3 portions into containers (fridge 3–4 days; the sauce alone also freezes well).

title: Mediterranean Lentil Soup (batch — plant-protein lunches)
ingredients: 1 large onion + 2 carrots + 3 celery stalks, diced small (or bell pepper + extra onion)
2 tsp cumin · 1 tsp cinnamon · plenty of black pepper — no salt
4 cups water + 4 cups low-sodium vegetable broth
To serve: Greek yogurt dollop, extra lemon

steps.text: Rinse lentils until water runs clear.
Sweat onion/carrot/celery in oil over medium-high, 6–7 min (skill: aromatics without burning).
Stir in garlic, cumin, cinnamon — 60 seconds until fragrant. Add lentils, toast 1–2 min.
Add liquid + lemon juice; boil, then simmer low **30–45 min** until lentils are tender.
Stir in kale to wilt. Taste: brighten with more lemon + pepper, not salt.
